plant.culled_by: TWO INDEPENDENT EYES. Rafe, device walk, 2026-09-06; and round 30's blind seat, 2026-09-06.
plant.verbatim: flat pale block, no interior texture (seat) / too shiny on worn areas, character washed out (Rafe)

seat.BEST_WHY: The wall-to-floor junction along the room's top wall (x 150–750, y ≈389–455) is stacked correctly and is the only piece of real construction anywhere in the set. Reading down a column at x≈260: mottled top surface from y 389 to y 422, then a hard 1px dark line at y≈423, then a course of cut blocks with legible vertical joints down to y≈455, then the floor. So the wall has a top, a face and a base, in that order, and you can tell where it stops. The repair timber and its driven pins sit *on that face* (the vertical beam at x≈297, y 423–455 with three short cross-pins) — where a pin would actually be driven — rather than floating in open masonry. Frames 1 and 4 invert this: blocks from y 393 to y 422, then soft brown cloud from y 422 down to the floor line, so the wall dissolves into the floor with no base edge at all.
seat.WORST_WHY: The frame contains at least two projections at once. The floor is straight-down orthographic — the grey slabs at y 217–267 are plain squares with no perspective, and the water at x 248–343 is a flat plane. But the two barrels at (113–143, 192–217) and (162–190, 192–217) are drawn from a raised 3/4 view: you see the full elliptical lid *and* the entire cylindrical side wall below it, about 25px of barrel body. The crates at x 63–97, y 2–90 are the same error — front-facing box faces with visible lid panels. Second: the dirt/water boundary is a dead-straight one-pixel vertical cut at x=248 running the full height y 0–192. No bank, no wet edge, no transition tile, no value shift on either side — two materials stickered together. Third, the grey floor band at y 217–267 is a uniform flat fill with a 1px grid and three scattered specks; it is not finished, it is a placeholder. Fourth, there is no light modelling of any kind in the frame — every surface is at full ambient, so nothing has a form.
seat.FLAGGED:
4, 2, 1, 3

- **4** — long parallel bright streaks laid over the floor from roughly (300,470) to (430,620) and (500,490) to (560,520). They are all at the same ~40° angle and they do not diverge, so they cannot be rays from the point light the figure is carrying; they cross tile joints without breaking. Alongside them, individual floor tiles are lit as whole units with hard tile-edge boundaries — e.g. the tile at (355–390, 460–490) is markedly brighter than its immediate neighbour with a straight vertical seam between them. Reads as a light layer painted on afterwards.
- **2** — the barrel/crate projection mismatch and the razor water edge, above. Both are a-glance obvious.
- **1 and 3** — the wall top surfaces, which are the largest single element in a top-down frame, carry no stonework at all. The corridor run at x 570–750, y 60–390 and the block at x 130–440, y 30–135 are soft brown blobs of varying size with a few thin dark scribbles over them. Zoomed or not, that region reads as blurred noise, not as the top of a masonry wall seen from above.

flip_list: Same as 1 for the wall top surfaces (x 570–750, y 60–390; x 130–440, y 30–135): cut them into blocks with varied joints instead of leaving noise blobs.
Same as 1 for the floor cracks: light them, and break them at the joints.

The value range across the lit room is compressed — the floor at (200,500), well inside the light, and the wall top at (620,300), well outside it, sit close enough in brightness that the light does not read as a light. Push the lit core up and the mid-falloff down so the carried lamp is legible as the only source.
The object at x 285–385, y 640–710 is the same rimless brown blob as in 1; give it a top face and a contact shadow or cut it.
Same as 1 for the sprite/background edge-hardness mismatch.
law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
